stories.title: Bybit accepts Franklin Templeton tokenized funds as trading collateral
stories.summary: Bybit now lets traders post Franklin Templeton's tokenized funds as collateral for trading. Franklin Templeton is extending its tokenized collateral service to the exchange. The move links a traditional asset manager's tokenized products directly to crypto exchange trading.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows a major asset manager and a large exchange deepening ties between tokenized real-world assets and crypto trading infrastructure.
whatToWatch: Whether other exchanges add similar tokenized-fund collateral options
Usage levels once the service is live
questions: What risk controls apply to this collateral if fund value moves sharply?
Will other fund issuers follow Franklin Templeton's lead?

stories.title: Nearly 5,000 BTC leaves Bitget as hackers begin laundering $387M haul
stories.summary: Attackers behind the roughly $387 million Bitget breach have started moving the stolen funds. Close to 5,000 BTC has already left wallets tied to the haul, marking the start of the laundering process.
stories.whyItMatters: The speed and scale of laundering test whether exchanges and chain-analysis firms can trace or freeze stolen funds before they disappear.
whatToWatch: Whether any of the moved BTC gets frozen or flagged by exchanges
Further large transfers from the hacker's wallets
questions: Which services or chains are being used to launder the funds?
How much, if any, of the haul can realistically be recovered?

stories.title: Citi and Coinbase partner to build stablecoin infrastructure for businesses
stories.summary: Citi and Coinbase are working together on stablecoin infrastructure aimed at business use, according to Bitcoin Magazine. Details on the specific product are still limited.
stories.whyItMatters: A major bank teaming up with a leading exchange on stablecoin rails signals continued mainstream adoption of stablecoins for commercial payments.
whatToWatch: Further details on the product and its launch timeline
Any regulatory sign-off needed for bank-linked stablecoin infrastructure
questions: What exactly are Citi and Coinbase building?
When might businesses be able to use it?

stories.title: Restaking's boom cools as top protocols barely turn a profit
stories.summary: The rapid growth phase for restaking protocols has ended, according to CoinDesk, with leading platforms now generating only thin profits. The sector's earlier rush of deposits and yield-seeking activity has slowed.
stories.whyItMatters: Restaking was one of DeFi's biggest yield narratives, so thinning margins suggest the sector is maturing or losing momentum, which matters for anyone tracking yield strategies.
whatToWatch: Whether protocols change fee models to improve margins
Signs of consolidation among restaking platforms
questions: Which specific protocols are most affected?
Is this a temporary slowdown or a structural decline?

stories.title: Strategy buys 1,665 more Bitcoin for $143M, lifting holdings to 847,666 BTC
stories.summary: Strategy purchased another 1,665 BTC for about $143 million, bringing its total Bitcoin holdings to 847,666 BTC. The company remains the largest known corporate holder of Bitcoin.
stories.whyItMatters: Continued large purchases by the biggest corporate Bitcoin holder are closely watched as a gauge of institutional demand.
whatToWatch: The next disclosed purchase and its size
How the buy was financed
questions: Is this purchase funded through debt, equity, or cash reserves?
How does it affect Strategy's average cost basis?

stories.title: Bitget reopens Bitcoin withdrawals after $387M hack, but ETH and USDT stay frozen
stories.summary: Bitget says Bitcoin withdrawals are open again following its roughly $387 million hack, while withdrawals of ETH and USDT remain paused. The exchange appears to be reopening access asset by asset rather than all at once.
stories.whyItMatters: A staggered reopening shows an exchange balancing user access against the risk of further illicit fund movement, a key test of trust after a breach.
whatToWatch: When ETH and USDT withdrawals resume
Further updates from Bitget on the investigation
questions: Why was BTC judged safe to reopen first?
What is the timeline for restoring other assets?

stories.title: Tom Lee's Bitmine buys another $47M in ETH, pushing stake to 4.9% of supply
stories.summary: Bitmine, chaired by Tom Lee, bought an additional $47 million of Ether, taking its total holdings to about 4.9% of Ethereum's circulating supply. The purchase continues the firm's aggressive ETH accumulation strategy.
stories.whyItMatters: Concentrating close to 5% of ETH supply in one company's hands mirrors corporate Bitcoin treasury strategies and raises questions about supply concentration.
whatToWatch: Further Bitmine ETH purchases
Whether holdings approach a larger share of total supply
questions: How is Bitmine funding these purchases?
Is this a long-term hold or an active trading position?

stories.title: Senate report says Tether's USDT is central to Iran's shadow banking network
stories.summary: A new Senate report identifies USDT as playing a central role in an Iranian shadow banking network, according to The Block. The report raises concerns about the stablecoin's use in sanctions evasion.
stories.whyItMatters: Tying the largest stablecoin issuer to sanctions-evasion allegations raises the likelihood of tighter regulatory and enforcement scrutiny on Tether.
whatToWatch: Tether's response to the report
Any Treasury or OFAC enforcement action that follows
questions: What specific evidence does the report cite?
Could this lead to penalties or new restrictions on Tether?

stories.title: SEC follows CFTC in issuing staff guidance for crypto
stories.summary: The US SEC has issued staff guidance on crypto, following similar guidance the CFTC released earlier, according to Cointelegraph. Details on the guidance's scope are still limited.
stories.whyItMatters: Coordinated guidance from the two main US market regulators could help clarify rules for crypto firms operating in areas that were previously unclear.
whatToWatch: What specific issues the guidance addresses once details emerge
Industry reaction and any follow-on rulemaking
questions: Is this guidance binding or purely informal?
Which parts of crypto markets does it cover?

stories.title: Bitget begins phased withdrawal resumption after $388M exploit
stories.summary: Bitget says it had roughly 30 minutes to contain its breach before about $290 million started moving, and the exchange has now begun a phased resumption of withdrawals following the $388 million exploit.
stories.whyItMatters: The short response window shows how fast attackers moved and puts Bitget's incident response and user communication under scrutiny.
whatToWatch: Full restoration of withdrawals across all assets
Any post-mortem or root-cause disclosure from Bitget
questions: What allowed the breach to happen?
Will affected users' funds be fully covered?

stories.title: THORChain refuses Bitget's request to block hacker as $6M moves to bitcoin
stories.summary: THORChain declined a request from Bitget to block the hacker behind its $387 million breach. About $6 million has already moved through THORChain into bitcoin.
stories.whyItMatters: The refusal highlights the tension between decentralized protocols' neutrality and exchanges' efforts to stop illicit funds from moving.
whatToWatch: Whether more stolen funds get routed through THORChain
Any legal or industry pressure on THORChain over the decision
questions: On what basis did Bitget make the blocking request?
What is THORChain's stated reasoning for refusing?

stories.title: Strategy makes first back-to-back Bitcoin buys since June
stories.summary: Strategy has made purchases on consecutive days for the first time since June, according to CryptoSlate. The pattern suggests the company's Bitcoin accumulation is picking up pace.
stories.whyItMatters: Back-to-back buying is watched as a signal of renewed confidence or acceleration in corporate Bitcoin demand.
whatToWatch: Whether the consecutive-day buying pattern continues
The next disclosed purchase amount
questions: What is driving the timing of these purchases?
Is the pace linked to a new financing round?
